title: Nettle seed tincture for adrenal fatigue
subtitle: A small-dose seed tincture for exhaustion and burnout recovery
excerpt: Fresh or dried nettle seed macerated in 40% vodka for four to six weeks to produce a small-dose adaptogenic tincture for adrenal fatigue, deep exhaustion, and burnout recovery. Five to ten drops in water twice daily. Different from all other nettle preparations: nettle seed is a distinct, more tonifying preparation than nettle leaf. Not for use alongside diuretic medication without supervision.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931) : Urtica dioica entry; nettle seed uses recorded. King's American Dispensatory (Felter and Lloyd, 1898) : Urtica dioica, tonic uses. Modern western herbal practice: nettle seed as an adrenal adaptogen is a contemporary western herbal framing, synthesised from practical herbalists working within the tradition (Matthew Wood, The Earthwise Herbal vol. 2, 2009 : nettle seed preparation for exhaustion; Robin Wall Kimmerer, Braiding Sweetgrass, 2013 : traditional ecological knowledge of nettle). The 1:2 fresh-seed ratio and the small (5 to 10 drop) dose follow herbalist consensus in contemporary UK practice rather than historic public-domain literature. SourceType SYNTHESISED reflects this. Safety notes from master herb row (not-with-diuretics-without-supervision).

recipe.yieldDescription: About 60 ml tincture (approximately 120 to 240 doses at 5 to 10 drops each)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Maceration takes 4 to 6 weeks. The finished tincture keeps 2 years in dark glass.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in amber glass in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps 2 years from the strain date.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation in which plant material is macerated in alcohol (usually 40% spirit) to extract both water-soluble and fat-soluble constituents. The alcohol also acts as a preservative, giving the preparation a shelf life of two years or more.

projectSchedule.title: Start your seed tincture
projectSchedule.body: If using fresh nettle seed: pack loosely into a clean maceration jar. Pour over the 40% vodka at a ratio of one part seed by weight to two parts spirit. If using dried seed: use one part seed to five parts spirit. The seed should be fully covered with at least 2 cm of liquid above. Seal and label with the herb name (nettle seed), the type (fresh or dried), the spirit percentage, and today's date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Check the liquid level
projectSchedule.body: Open the jar and check the spirit still covers the seed. Top up with a little more 40% vodka if needed. Fresh seed may absorb more liquid as it softens. Shake gently and return to the cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Taste and check colour
projectSchedule.body: Taste a few drops from a small spoon. The tincture should have a mild, grassy, slightly earthy flavour. It should be a pale green-brown colour. Return to the cupboard for another two weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Your tincture is ready. Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent seed firmly. Funnel into a small amber dropper bottle. Label with the herb and part (nettle seed), the spirit percentage, and the strain date. Note the small dose on the label: 5 to 10 drops per dose.

content.text: Nettle seed
tincture

is a preparation from the seed of the common stinging nettle, not from the leaf. The seed preparation is distinct from all other nettle preparations in the herbal library: where nettle leaf is traditionally used as a nutritive and a mild helps the body pass water, nettle seed is used in modern western herbal practice as a small-dose tonic for adrenal fatigue and deep exhaustion following sustained stress or illness. The dose is small: five to ten drops in water twice daily. This is not a preparation where more is better; the seed is potent at this scale. Fresh seed is preferred where available, at a ratio of one part seed to two parts 40% spirit. Dried seed works well too, at one part to five parts spirit. The
tincture
keeps two years in dark glass.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. helps the body pass water: nettle seed is less helps the body pass water than nettle leaf, but it still carries a mild helps the body pass water effect. Readers on prescription helps the body pass water (furosemide, bumetanide, or similar) should consult their prescriber before using this preparation. This is a small-dose preparation; do not exceed 10 drops per dose or two doses per day. No pregnancy safety data for nettle seed at therapeutic tincture doses; consult a herbalist or your midwife before use in pregnancy or breastfeeding. This preparation is sourced from modern western herbal practice; it is a traditional-use preparation without randomised clinical-trial evidence.

attrs.title: About the source for this preparation
attrs.body: Nettle seed as an adrenal tonic is a contemporary western herbal framing. It is not found in the 17th-century herbalist Nicholas Culpeper or Maud Grieve, the early 20th-century botanical writer, in this specific form. the preparation has developed within modern western herbal practice over the past few decades. The master herb row for nettle in this library is sourced from western herbal tradition broadly. the seed tincture at small doses is presented here as a traditional-use preparation without clinical-trial evidence. The sourceType is SYNTHESISED to reflect this.

content.text: Ingredients

items.prepNote: fresh nettle seed (green, from late summer harvest). If using dried seed, use 12 g dried seed to 60 ml spirit instead.
plain 40% vodka (fresh seed: 1:2 ratio; dried seed: 1:5 ratio)

content.text: Method
Step 1: Pack and cover

Pack the fresh nettle seed loosely into a small, clean soaking period jar. Pour over the 40% vodka until the seed is fully submerged with at least 2 cm of liquid above. For dried seed, use 12 g dried seed to 60 ml 40% vodka. Seal tightly. Label with the herb and part (nettle seed), the spirit percentage, and today's date.
Step 2: Macerate four to six weeks
Store in a cool, dark cupboard. Shake every few days. After two weeks, check the liquid level. At four weeks, taste a few drops: the
tincture
should be mild and grassy. Leave up to six weeks for a complete extraction.
Step 3: Strain and bottle
Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent seed firmly. Funnel the strained
tincture
into a small amber dropper bottle. Note on the label: five to ten drops per dose.
Dosing

Five to ten drops (from the dropper) in a small glass of water, twice daily. This is a microdose preparation: the small dose is intentional and is not meant to be increased. Morning and early afternoon work well. Course: three months is the standard course for adrenal support. After three months, take a break of at least four weeks before considering another course. If energy does not improve after six to eight weeks, consult a herbalist.
Storage
Store in amber glass dropper bottles in a cool, dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the strain date.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you are on prescription helps the body pass water medication without consulting your prescriber first. Consult a herbalist or your midwife before use in pregnancy or while breastfeeding. See a doctor for persistent fatigue lasting more than a few weeks. Fatigue with weight loss or gain, fatigue with breathlessness or chest pain, or fatigue that does not improve with rest. Adrenal fatigue as a home-remedy complaint is distinct from medical adrenal insufficiency, which needs diagnosis and treatment from a doctor.
